description: Takımımız lisede Teknofest Roket Yarışması Lise Kategorisi için kurulmuş ve 2 yıllık yoğun çalışmanın sonucu olarak yarışmada Türkiye Birincisi olmaya hak kazanmıştır. Şimdi ise takım üyeleri olarak Nasa Space Apps Challenge için tekrar bir araya gelerek yarışmaya katılıyoruz.
summary: Etügen is a mobile-first web application that transforms 25 years of NASA Earth observation data into plain-language, actionable 2-to-3-year crop rotation and irrigation plans for any field on Earth. By combining satellite climate records, soil moisture, terrain elevation, and agronomic physics (FAO-56) without opaque "black-box" AI, it empowers farmers to adapt their crop cycles to shifting climate conditions in seconds—while transparently displaying data confidence, water deficits, and contour-planting guidance.
details:
The Problem

While climate patterns are shifting beneath farmers' feet, traditional crop rotations often remain static. NASA holds decades of high-resolution precipitation, temperature, soil moisture, vegetation, and terrain data for every field on Earth, yet a smallholder farmer cannot easily translate raw satellite archives into practical answers to "What should I sow, when should I sow it, and how much water will I need?"

Our Solution

Etügen bridges the gap between raw satellite telemetry and field-level decisions in three simple steps—with zero farming jargon in its default Easy Mode:

  1. Locate & Measure: The user selects their field on a satellite map and optionally marks its corners to calculate exact area in decares.
  2. Irrigation Check: The user answers a single question regarding irrigation availability (No / Limited / Yes).
  3. Actionable 2–3 Year Rotation Plan: Within ~3–4 seconds, the app generates a tailored multi-year crop cycle (e.g., Barley → Lentil) detailing optimal sowing and harvest windows, expected seasonal rainfall deficits (in mm and total tons of water for the field), and exact irrigation intervals during peak water-demand periods.

Key Features & Engineering Rigor

  • Contour Planting Guidance (NASADEM): Using terrain elevation data, the app determines the field's slope direction and visually instructs the farmer to sow rows perpendicular to the slope to minimize soil erosion and maximize water infiltration.
  • Expert Mode: Agronomists and power users can switch to Expert Mode to inspect 9 transparent sub-scores (Yield Suitability, Bad-Year Resilience, Water Balance, Soil Health Proxy, Nitrogen Balance, Family Diversity, etc.), customize constraints, and review the scientific evidence behind every card.
  • Validation Against Ground & Satellite Truth: Rather than blindly trusting models, we cross-checked outputs against MODIS phenology and real-world agricultural trials across three distinct demo regions: Konya (Türkiye), Punjab (India), and Nakuru (Kenya). For example, calibrating with 2023–24 Punjab Agricultural University local cultivar trials reduced maturity prediction gaps, while cross-checking NASA POWER against CHIRPS flagged a 1.8× rainfall discrepancy in Konya—prompting automatic user warnings and alternative rain sources.
  • Responsible & Privacy-First Design: Unknown parameters are explicitly labeled as "missing data" rather than fabricated. Every recommendation includes confidence indicators and prompts to consult local agricultural engineers. Furthermore, exact field polygons never leave the user's device; the server only processes coordinates rounded to ~5 km.

Tech Stack & Development Tools

  • Languages & Frontend: Built as a responsive, mobile-first web application using TypeScript and CSS for the interactive satellite map interface, polygon area calculation, and Easy/Expert mode switching, paired with Python for satellite data processing, agronomic physics modeling (FAO-56 evapotranspiration, water deficit, and slope calculations), and multi-criteria crop rotation scoring.
  • Licensing & Privacy: Open-sourced under the Apache-2.0 license. Exact field boundaries remain strictly client-side; only coordinates rounded to ~5 km are queried.

Super Intelligence (SI) / AI Usage Disclosure

  • In accordance with NASA Space Apps Challenge guidelines, generative AI tools were utilized strictly as a development assistant for code refactoring, debugging, translating/editing UI and presentation text, and structuring documentation. All agronomic formulas, satellite data pipelines, validation metrics, and physical rules in the core recommendation engine are deterministic and grounded in peer-reviewed scientific standards (no black-box ML/AI).
dataRefs: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources)
NASA MODIS (NDVI & Land Cover Dynamics / Phenology)
projectRefs: CHIRPS (Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Station data)
